gen-nosifer-fs-ranade: Dark and slow, Nosifer spaces its pinched, crayon-thick letters wide. Ranade follows in a plain sans whose weight barely wobbles, so a long page keeps moving with a gentle, organic drift.
gen-nosifer-fs-supreme: Heavy, sealed-shut lettering with a menacing grin. Supreme takes over in sans-serif with open, crisp shapes and a dense strip of text, so long paragraphs read cleanly after Nosifer's gloom.
gen-nosifer-general-sans: Nosifer looks like melting crayon, spaced wide and pinched tight at every mouth, while General Sans runs smooth and unobstructed with a big x-height. Hard to miss the difference.
gen-nosifer-satoshi: Pinched, crayon-fat lowercase with a slow, widely tracked stride gives Nosifer its menace, while Satoshi offers a soaring x-height and open e shapes in sans form. They split the page between dread and ease.
gen-nosifer-switzer: Tall, thick crayon-like lowercase with sealed, pinched mouths defines Nosifer, giving every heading a slow and ominous stride. Switzer then slips in beneath with wire-like sans-serif letters and open c tips, making the whole page feel suddenly lighter.
gen-nosifer-work-sans: Waxy, pinched and spread wide, Nosifer sets a dark scene, while Work Sans keeps its pencil pressure constant and its mean line high. One makes a spectacle; the other simply keeps reading easy.
gen-orbitron-gf-cascadia-mono: Wide-spaced letters with generous eyes on every e define Orbitron. Cascadia Mono sits below in compact sans-serif, with curves as thick as its stems, and the two make a tidy, machine-like page.
gen-orbitron-gf-julius-sans-one: Orbitron stretches its open-aperture letters far apart along the line, while Julius Sans One uses almost matching capital and lowercase heights with wide gaps between letters. Both share a spacious feel.
gen-orbitron-gf-lexend-exa: Spacious, precise, almost engineered. Lexend Exa carries the text in sans-serif with uniform stroke thickness and a big x-height, giving Orbitron's spread-out headings a sturdy, open partner underneath.
gen-orbitron-gf-lexend-giga: Orbitron looks precise, widely spaced and wide-eyed. It excels at crisp headline impact, while Lexend Giga, a plain sans of flat linework and generous tracking, quietly handles the body text.
